notes: fresh start: no spec, no prior run for this branch
4 commits + lint ignore; D16 admin sign-in FAIL (prod-only Clerk), data path verified

events.detail: hellokahwin BMAD engine is 6.10.0 (main checkout, untracked, absent from worktree) vs library 6.12.0

notes.text: `ua-parser-js@^2` ships its own types (`src/main/ua-parser.d.ts`), so `@types/ua-parser-js@^0.7.39` (the v0.7 API) is redundant and may disagree with the v2 types. The spec asks for it explicitly, so this is not a finding.
The rate limit runs before the salt check, so with `ANALYTICS_SALT` missing, a client over 120/min gets 429 rather than 503. Harmless.
The salt check runs after body validation, so with the salt missing a malformed body gets 400, not 503. A well-formed request still gets 503 plus an error log, which satisfies CAP-3.
If none of the IP headers is present, every request hashes as `'unknown'`. Vercel always sets `x-real-ip`, and the earlier review already rejected this concern.
`pathname` is required (1–2000 chars) at the API, while the DB column is nullable. This is stricter than the spec in a harmless direction.
`screen_width` is capped at 10000. The spec states no upper bound; this is stricter and harmless.
When the store is full and every bucket is live, eviction sorts all 10k entries on each new IP. The earlier review accepted this.
The `keySuffix` option is beyond spec scope, and the collector does not use it.

The migration matches the spec's DB block. Indexes add an explicit `USING btree` (the default). Running D12's grep finds one `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` and no DROP or ALTER of other tables, and the journal has `idx: 5, tag: 0005_analytics_events`.
`region_source`, `city_source` and the `visitor_created` partial index are dropped, as the design notes require. The schema is exported from `schema/index.ts:11`.
Not part of this chunk. Checked at HEAD: `isClerkRoute` still leaves out the collect route, as the constraint requires.
Ignoring `_bmad/**` and `.tmp-ops/**` matches the decisions file. It is outside the spec's capabilities and has no impact on them.
The bound test runs 10,001 iterations and would fail if eviction went back to expired-only. It is a real test, just slow-ish.

D5's check that no part of the IP appears in the hash is weak. A hex digest can never contain `.`, so the dotted-fragment loop and `not.toContain('.')` can't fail once the 64-hex test passes. Only `not.toContain(ip)` is a real check. Digit-only fragments such as `203` or `113` can't be asserted absent from a hex string anyway.

On the client, `decodeURIComponent(match[1])` has no try/catch. A malformed `_hk_vid` cookie such as `%zz` would throw a URIError inside `track()` or a click handler, which is exactly the failure `uuid.ts` was written to avoid. This is a robustness issue, not a spec gap.

No test checks the cookie attributes CAP-3 requires: `Max-Age` of 2 years, `Path=/`, `SameSite=Lax`, and `Secure` on https. `tracker.test.ts:83` only checks that a UUID-shaped `_hk_vid` exists. jsdom hides those attributes from `document.cookie`, so checking them would need a spy on the cookie setter.
`VISITOR_ID_RE` accepts any 8-4-4-4-12 hex string, case-insensitive, not only v4 UUIDs. That's harmless because the column type is `uuid`, and it meets CAP-3's "UUID".

The country from `x-vercel-ip-country` and `cf-ipcountry` is stored without upper-casing or validation, so `XX`, `T1` and similar values reach the table. The read side's `parseCountry` filters them for drill-down, but they can still show up as their own rows in the Countries panel. The spec only requires that the header populates the row.

The tests assert latitude but never longitude. They also don't cover a non-numeric latitude/longitude header becoming null, or a malformed percent-sequence in the city header falling back to the raw value.

`device.ts`, `uuid.ts` and `visitor-id.ts` have no unit test files of their own, although the Auto Run Result lists the whole group as "(+ tests)". Coverage does exist elsewhere: `parseDevice` and `parseVisitorIdCookie` through `collect/__tests__/route.test.ts:115,199`, and the `randomUuid` fallback and cookie minting through `tracker.test.ts:81,223`.

`package.json` pairs `ua-parser-js ^2.0.10`, which ships its own types, with `@types/ua-parser-js ^0.7.39`, which describes v1. The spec requires both, and the named `UAParser` import works with v2. The v1 type package is probably redundant (`package.json` is outside this chunk).

The bare `whatsapp` pattern marks every UA containing "WhatsApp" as `social:whatsapp`. The link-preview fetcher sends `WhatsApp/2.x`, but if the WhatsApp in-app webview ever adds that token, real visitors would be counted as bots. This is the same class of bug as the Pinterest fix; none was observed here.
The heuristic that flags desktop-Linux Chrome as a bot (`heuristic:datacenter_linux_chrome`) also catches real Linux desktop Chrome users. The triage log accepts this for parity with twn-new.
D2 expects `bot_reason` to start with `search_engine` "(or the ported reason prefix)". The ported prefix is `search:`, so Googlebot gets `search:googlebot`, which falls within the allowance.
The comments still describe twn-new's `/wa/` WhatsApp-click audit, which doesn't exist in hellokahwin. They're inherited from the port and only affect wording.

Nothing tests that the `visibilitychange: hidden` listener calls `flush()`. The `sendBeacon` test sets `visibilityState` and then calls `flush()` directly, so the CAP-2 "flush on visibilitychange" wiring has no test.

The `/draft/` guard in `enqueue()` reads `window.location.pathname`, not the pathname passed in. `trackPageview('/draft/x')` called from a non-draft URL would still be queued. The only caller, `AnalyticsTracker`, guards first, so nothing goes wrong today.
`sendBeacon`'s `false` return is ignored, so a refused beacon is lost silently. This was already triaged and rejected in the spec's review log.
Every in-session pageview sends the landing `document.referrer`, because `trackPageview` falls back to it when no referrer is passed. This matches twn-new and was already triaged and rejected.
Re-renders on the same pathname (for example a query-only change) are deliberately not counted as pageviews. This matches CAP-2's "pathname change" wording.

The tracker is mounted as a `<Suspense>` sibling of `<main>{children}</main>`, not a wrapper, as the constraint requires. `/login`, `/no-access`, `(admin-preview)` and `(print)` all sit outside `(public)`, so they are excluded because of where the tracker is mounted.

Article titles are looked up by slug only. The category segment and publish status are not checked, so `/artikel/<wrong-cat>/<slug>` resolves to the article's title. Slugs are UNIQUE, so the title is correct, but the path might not have rendered that page.
`/brand` resolves to the English "Brand". The spec lists `/brand` without a Malay label, so this is consistent with the constraint "Malay labels where a static route has one".
Each lookup is wrapped in `Promise.allSettled`, so if one type fails, that type falls back to the raw path and nothing is logged. That is safe for display, but the failure is invisible.

The `/draft/abc` component test works because jsdom's `window.location` stays at `/`. The component's own guard is the only thing that stops the event, so the test would fail if that guard were removed.

`total_pageviews` only counts pageviews that have a `session_id`, so pageview rows without a session are dropped from the Pageviews tile and from views/visit. The tracker always sets `session_id`, so in practice only hand-posted beacons like P9's curl are affected. That fits the spec's "visit = session" definition, but the Pageviews tile is not a raw count of pageview rows.

A session that holds only custom events (no pageview) counts as a visit but never as a bounce, which lowers the bounce rate slightly. This matches twn-new's definition (bounce = exactly one pageview).

`getChartData` always returns one zero-filled point per day, so an empty range comes back as all zeros, never as an empty array. Whether CAP-7's empty state still shows depends on `dashboard.tsx` treating "all zeros" as empty. That file is outside this chunk.

The referrer-host regex removes the scheme, `www.` and anything from the first `/`. A port (`host:8080`), or a query string on a referrer with no path (`https://x.com?a=1`), stays in the name. That is the same as twn-new; browsers usually send an origin plus `/`, so it rarely shows.
`pct` divides by the sum of the top-20 rows, not by all distinct visitors. Earlier triage accepted this as twn-new parity.
`searchPages` ignores the country and region scope (accepted as an admin convenience in earlier triage). It is date-bounded and escapes LIKE wildcards correctly.
`scope()` applies `regionFilter` even when there is no country. CAP-10's "region only with a country" is enforced instead in `page.tsx:88`, which drops `region` when `country` is absent.

`countryFilter` only checks the alpha-2 shape, so pseudo-codes like `XX` would pass. That is safe today because `page.tsx` runs `parseCountry` first and drops them, but the filter does not guard against them itself.
`regionFilter` does not upper-case its input. It depends on `parseRegion` having normalised the value first, which `page.tsx` does.

`AT TIME ZONE` only appears in a SELECT, for day bucketing. Every WHERE compares the bare `created_at` with bound `::timestamptz` parameters, which meets the query-discipline constraint. Top stats and the chart both use `WITH scoped AS MATERIALIZED`.

The header says the file is "Ported verbatim" from The Wedding Notebook, but it adds `MAX_RANGE_DAYS`, `resolveRange` and `isBoundedRange`. These came from the review patch (VG-3/VG-9). The behaviour matches CAP-12; only the "verbatim" label in the design-notes table is no longer accurate.

When `from` is after `to`, `resolveRange` resets both ends to the default 30-day window rather than falling back only the bad param. CAP-12 says invalid dates "fall back" and does not cover from > to, so this is a reasonable reading.
`runBatched` runs 17 thunks, not the "16 getters" in the design notes. The extra one is the second `getCachedTopStats` call for the previous period. There are still 16 distinct getters.
Countries is global over geo but still filtered by `page` and `traffic`. That fits both CAP-10 ("stays global" as the navigator) and CAP-9 ("every panel honours" `?page=`).
With no country selected, States skips the query and returns `[]`. CAP-10 scopes States to a country, so an empty panel without one is consistent.

The `?page=` value reaches the cache key and `pageFilter` without any length bound or normalisation. It is admin-only and goes through bound parameters, so there is no injection risk, but every distinct value creates a new cache entry.
Page search does not take country or region. This was already raised and rejected in triage (BH-13). CAP-9 only asks for the search to be bounded by the date range.

The cache uses tag `site-analytics` and `revalidate: 600`, and the getter args are folded into the key implicitly, as CAP-15 requires. Nothing in the repo calls `revalidateTag('site-analytics')`, so the 10-minute TTL is the only way entries go stale.

The 16 ISO 3166-2:MY codes match the standard (`01` Johor … `16` Putrajaya). The admin UI uses the Malay state names (e.g. "Wilayah Persekutuan Kuala Lumpur", "Pulau Pinang"); CAP-10 only gives `10` → Selangor as an example.
This test fails if the change is reverted, because the module would be missing. Its assertions check real mapping and fallback behaviour, so it can fail on a wrong implementation.
Passing `size <= 0` would loop forever. The only caller passes 4, and triage already rejected this as a false positive.

The scoped-getter test does check CAP-12's discipline: bare `created_at` compared with `>=` and `<` against `::timestamptz` parameters, no `<=`, no `AT TIME ZONE` after `WHERE`, and the exact UTC bounds for the KL days.
`sql.split('WHERE')[1]` only looks at the text after the first `WHERE`, so a zone-wrapped `created_at` in a later `WHERE` would go unnoticed. `getCities` has only one `WHERE`, so it is fine here.
No test checks top stats: the `WITH scoped AS MATERIALIZED` constraint or the CAP-6 definitions (bounce, the 1800s duration cap, distinct `visitor_hash`). This chunk doesn't claim to test them.
The "`?region=` only honoured with a country" rule lives in `page.tsx:88` and has no test in this chunk.
The `getChartData` zero-fill test covers the CAP-7 per-KL-day points, including days with no data.
The D9 assertions match the spec exactly. The test also covers all nine provider pseudo-codes from CAP-10.
The `countryFilter` sanity test sits inside the `regionFilter` describe block. This is only about organisation.
The D8 assertions match the spec's values exactly. `resolveRange` covers the CAP-12 30-day default, clamping `to` to today, falling back when from > to, and the 366-day clamp.
`resolveRange` is tested with a local-midnight `Date` that stands in for `getKLToday()`. `getKLToday()` itself (the `toLocaleDateString` path for the KL zone) is not tested.
Checks that order is kept and peak concurrency equals the batch size. Size ≤ 0 is not tested; the triage log already rejected that case as unreachable.
Covers the auth gate and the bounded-range rejection. Neither query-whitespace trimming nor how `traffic` is parsed when passed to `searchPages` is checked.
`regionHref` builds a region link even when there is no country in the search string. The page ignores such a region (`page.tsx:88`), so it causes no harm, but no test covers it.

The six KPI tiles are hand-built buttons, not `StatCard`. `StatCard` has no `onClick` or pressed state, only a link, so it can't do CAP-7's click-to-switch chart. That reason holds, but nothing in the code records it.
`DataTable` is a custom bar-list, not `ConsoleTable`. It reads like twn-new's panel UI. The spec's success criteria only say "tables", so I left this as a note.

The chart empty state is `chartData.every(d => d.unique_visitors === 0)`. That is true for an empty array, so an empty range shows the empty state and doesn't crash. This meets CAP-7 and matches the zero-fill comment.
The "30 minutes of inactivity" session text matches `SESSION_TIMEOUT_MS` in `tracker.ts:22`. The 30-minute duration cap matches CAP-6's 1800s.
It adds a "UTM Source" tab on top of CAP-8's three acquisition tables. This came from the triage patch for the success signal and goes beyond scope.

The Locations panel's `key` resets the tab to one level below the current drill. "Countries" always renders the global `countries` prop, and States shows a prompt when no country is set. This is consistent with CAP-10; whether the data is scoped correctly is decided in `queries.ts`/`page.tsx`, outside this chunk.
Country names come from `Intl.DisplayNames` and are gated by `isCountryCode`, so pseudo-codes like `XX` render raw (CAP-10).
When the previous period is 0 it shows an em-dash instead of a percentage. `higherIsBetter=false` on Bounce Rate turns a rise red. Neither is set by the spec; both are sensible.
It uses the existing `LoadingRows` primitive plus raw `animate-pulse` divs. The repo has no `Skeleton` component, so nothing is left unused.

No test renders `dashboard.tsx` or `change-badge.tsx`. The "dashboard href test" from triage is in `__tests__/drill-down.test.ts`, which tests `drill-down.ts`, not this component. No dev check claims coverage of these files, so this isn't a false-verification finding.

The test "keeps Articles first" still passes if the change is reverted. It doesn't check anything about CAP-13; it's a regression guard for the `/admin` redirect target and can only fail if someone reorders the groups. The other three tests in this file would fail on revert (href present, `findGroupForPath` returns `analytics`, ⌘K "traffic" finds it), so D11 is genuinely tested.
No test checks the group's icon (`BarChart3Icon`), its label "Analytics", or the full keyword string. The code matches the spec on all three.

"Rolled-over dates fall back" and "range > 366 clamps" (CAP-12) are left to the server (`resolveRange`). The custom form only blocks from>to and to>today, so someone can submit a 2-year range and the server quietly shortens it to 366 days. The earlier triage rejected that as spec'd behaviour.

Applying a preset or custom range keeps the existing `page`, `country`, `region` and `traffic` params. That fits "every panel honours it", but a chosen page stays filtered even when it has no rows in the new range.
The preset match is a plain from/to comparison. On the 1st of a month, "Today" and "This month" give the same range, and the label always shows "Today" (first match wins). This is cosmetic only.
The search sends from/to/traffic but not country/region, so the results can include pages with no rows in the current geo scope. The earlier triage rejected this as admin convenience.
The 300ms debounce timer is never cleared on unmount, so one stray server-action call can happen after navigation. The earlier triage rejected this as harmless.
Picking a page doesn't drop `country`/`region`, so the page filter is applied on top of any active geo drill-down. This fits the spec, but the chip doesn't mention the geo scope.
`formatCount` uses `toFixed(1)`, so 999,950 and above shows as "1000.0k". The earlier triage rejected this as unreachable at hellokahwin's traffic.

The toggle has no tests. CAP-4 (labels show distinct-visitor counts per bucket, switching changes every panel) relies on page.tsx passing the `trafficCounts` it computes and on the server re-reading `?traffic=`. Both live outside this chunk, and P5 checks them in prod.
The Analytics group sits between Media and Design rather than at the end. The spec doesn't say where it should go. The single-tab group not showing in the tab bar is already known and accepted.

blind.reason: risk override: diff adds a DB migration/schema and handles visitor privacy data

edge.reason: risk override; diff also adds parsing, validation, rate limiting and date arithmetic

acceptance.reason: risk override; spec has 15 capabilities plus orchestrator decisions

review.reviewer_summary: policy: claude primary (config/review-policy.json); all three layers on claude-opus-5-5 at rung 0, no Codex account touched; each layer split into 8 chunks (24 blind headless sessions, 8 concurrent) because the reviewable diff is ~5,486 lines after excluding pnpm-lock.yaml and the generated 0005_snapshot.json; edge-layer MEDIUM mapped to major and LOW to minor.
review.note: diff.files/lines are the full stat excluding pnpm-lock.yaml (8375+/5-); the 2,894-line generated drizzle snapshot was not handed to reviewers. Per-layer seconds are summed chunk wall times (chunks ran 8-wide in parallel; whole review wall time ~2.7 min). Several findings (F16, F23, F24, F35, F38-F40, F46) touch items the spec triage log previously rejected as twn-new parity or unreachable; they were raised blind and are recorded as-is; the fixer may rebut. Fix-check 1: F26 was written REBUTTAL_ACCEPTED by the fix-check, but its evidence says it is a fix and should read CLOSED; recorded as closed (fixer class defect-edge, not an override). Severity counts now reflect open findings only. Fix-check 2 (scoped to F17, delta 8d61eaf..cf307ad): CLOSED.
